semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Performing the spiral acquisition
After you changed scan parameters, you must confirm the new settings with Load before starting the scan.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30
6 Examination
If the spiral is part of an auto range and not all ranges have been selected at least once, a parameter overview is displayed. You can display this overview manually with View
> Examination Overview... .
1 Click the Load button to confirm the scan parameters.
As soon as you click the Load button, the topogram is zoomed and moved in a way that the whole planned scan range is displayed.
2 Press the MOVE key on the control box until table movement stops.
– or –
Click the Cancel Move button to begin the spiral at the current table position.
3 Press the START key on the control box.
You can observe the progress of your scan on the screen:
In the chronicle, you can see the remaining scan time.
In the topogram, the current scan position is displayed.
In the tomo segment, the calculated tomograms are displayed.
RTD (Real Time Display) images are reconstructed to observe the scan progress.
4 Use the MOVE key to move to the starting position of the next range.
5 Begin with the next scan.
– or –
Reconstruct the scan series with full image quality.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 319
6 Examination
6 Conclude the examination by creating a topographic image. For how to proceed: ( Page 326 Reconstruction), ( Page 331 Concluding an Examination)

section.title: Defining different cycle times
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Scan/Acquiring an Adaptive 4D spiral/Defining different cycle times

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Defining different cycle times
You can define different cycle times for one Adaptive 4D Spiral scan in the Cycle time table dialog box.
The values that are displayed in No of scans and Cycle time are derived from the scan protocol or the current scan entry. You can change these entries and add more entries.
Already scanned entries are dimmed.
The Cycle time table dialog box is open.
1 Enter how many scans have to be performed with a specified cycle time into the No of scans field.
2 Specify the cycle time in the Cycle time field.
3 Repeat this for each cycle time. You can define up to ten cycle times.
4 Select the Apply check boxes for all cycle times that you want to scan.
5 Click OK .
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30
6 Examination
To synchronize the reconstruction of the images (displayed in the tomo segment) with scanning, you can increase the cycle time.
You can use the Cycle time table also for certain scan protocols without table feed, for example, non-gated perfusion sequence scans.

section.title: Selecting a metal implant
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Reconstruction/Performing a reconstruction with reduced metal artifacts (iMAR)/Selecting a metal implant

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Selecting a metal implant
A kernel that supports iMAR is selected.
1 On the Recon parameter card, click the Advanced reconstruction options icon.
The Advanced reconstruction options dialog box opens.
2 From the iMAR list, select an implant.
3 Click the Advanced reconstruction options icon again to close the Artifact correction dialog box.
To deactivate iMAR, select None from the iMAR list.
4 Start the reconstruction. See ( Page 329 Starting reconstruction).
The following labels are displayed in the image comment area of the reconstructed images:
For Neuro coils: iMARne
For Dental fillings: iMARde
For Spine implants: iMARsp
For Shoulder implants: iMARsh
For Pacemaker: iMARpa
For Thoracic coils: iMARth
For Hip implants: iMARhi
For Extremity implants: iMARex
Series descriptions
For Series descriptions of iMAR recon jobs, the following suffix is added:
iMAR
The suffix is not shown in the Recon parameter card.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: 6.7.11 Optimizing the image display
Image series requirements for the 3D GRP Base are:
Extended FoV is off
Center X, Center Y, and FoV are the same for all images of the series
1 Select a segment.
2 Click the following icons from the tool bar on the Examination or on the Recon task card.
3 Click the Free Mode icon if you want to rotate the axes in any segment.
4 Click the Default Orientation icon if you want to set the orientation of the 3D Recon segments to their defaults.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 340
6 Examination
5 Click the Hide Reference Lines icon if you want to suppress the cutlines in the 3D Recon segments.
6 Click the MPR Thick and MIP Thin icons if you want to select the image type for the 3D GRP Base.
7 Click the Set FoV Segment icon if you want to define the active 3D Recon segment as new FoV segment.
8 Click the Set Reference Segment icon if you want to define the active segment as new segment for the reference image. Zoom, pan, and window the image.
9 Click the Preview Image icon if you want to check whether the reconstruction parameters you set are suitable.
10 Select an existing 3D GRP Base from the Planning base selection list for the current and the following 3D recon jobs.
11 From the Matrix Size selection list, select a FoV matrix for the 3D reconstruction of spiral scans.
Auto: The system determines the optimum matrix size according to FoV and kernel.
For each matrix, choose the format:
Square: The FoV is quadratic.
Non square: You can adjust the FoV as a rectangle according to your needs.
If you use the non-square matrix and extend the side length of your FoV to more than the maximum ratio, the shorter side is stretched so that the maximum ratio applies again.
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
6 Examination
12 From the Planning base selection list, select an existing image series for the oblique recon jobs. Only images with a resolution below or equal to 512 are supported as a planning base.

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: 7.1.1 Activating Bolus Tracking
You can use Bolus Tracking for most of the diagnostic scan modes.

The scan parameters of the diagnostic scan are used to determine the parameter settings of the PreMonitoring and Monitoring scan. If the parameters of the monitoring scan and diagnostic scan differ, the system will increase the delay time between monitoring scans and diagnostic scans.
You can only activate Bolus Tracking if the scan you selected was not examined yet.
1 Select the diagnostic scan entry you want to scan with Bolus Tracking in the chronicle.
2 Right-click the diagnostic scan entry and select Bolus Tracking from the context menu.
All the examination steps required for Bolus Tracking are displayed in the chronicle.

section.title: Activating the coupled mode
section.hierarchy_path: /Enhanced examination/CARE Contrast CT/Activating the coupled mode

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: 7.2.1 Activating the coupled mode

You can couple the CT scanner and the bolus injector so that you can start and stop both systems, and transfer the injection parameters between the two systems. The scanner gets extended operational control over the bolus injector. The scanner is able to retrieve information from the bolus injector about the applied injection.
If you paste or repeat a coupled range, the new range is reset to uncoupled.
You can see the status of the bolus injector by different icons in the status bar of the monitor:
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 350
7 Enhanced examination
By selecting Edit > Save Scan Protocol from the main menu, you can save scan protocols with Injector coupled as predefined scan start.
Scan ranges are marked within the chronicle to distinguish an unscanned from an already finished or uncoupled scan range.

Icon | Meaning
 | Bolus injector coupling rejected
 | Bolus injector available
 | Bolus injector ready
 | Local procedure on bolus injector active

Icon | Meaning
 | Coupled unscanned scan range
 | Coupled scanned scan range
 | Uncoupled scan range
 | Coupled unscanned scan range with FAST Bolus
 | Coupled scanned scan range with FAST Bolus

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Autoranges in coupled mode
In an autorange, select the Injector coupled setting for the first scan range only. The injector is automatically coupled for all remaining ranges.
If you suspend the scan in an autorange, the injection is canceled immediately for the current scan range.

section.title: Defining the start delay
section.hierarchy_path: /Enhanced examination/CARE Contrast CT/Checking the parameter settings/Defining the start delay

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Defining the start delay

You can perform a TestBolus scan with a small amount of contrast medium to define the start delay. Therefore choose TestBolus from the context menu of the chronicle. Load the acquired images in syngo Dynamic Evaluation to evaluate the time to peak enhancement. This time can then be used as the optimal start delay time for the diagnostic scan.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30
7 Enhanced examination
CAUTION
Misunderstanding of reference point for start delay in bolus examination!
Faulty synchronization between bolus and scanning.
◆ Make sure that the chosen delay time fits to the characteristics of the bolus injection.
◆ Enter the required scan delay time in the Delay entry field.
On the Contrast parameter card, the delay is updated accordingly (read-only).
